description: This sunburst chart, functioning as a multi-level pie chart, represents a hierarchical classification of language data across three concentric rings. The innermost ring divides the total dataset into two primary categories: "Abusive," colored in teal and occupying approximately 55% to 60% of the chart, and "Not Abusive," colored in yellow-orange and taking up the remaining 40% to 45%. The middle ring further subdivides these primary categories into specific topics, maintaining the respective teal and yellow-orange color schemes of their parent slices. Within the "Abusive" section, the middle ring contains five slices labeled "Political," "Racial," "Sexist," "Religious" (a very narrow sliver), and "Other," which appears to be the largest segment in this group. The "Not Abusive" section's middle ring is similarly divided into "Other" (the largest segment), "Political," "Religious," and extremely thin slivers for "Sexist" and "Racial." The outermost ring provides a third level of classification, breaking down the middle ring's topics into sentiments or stances such as "Negative," "Positive," "Mixed," and "Neutral," utilizing lighter shades of teal and pale yellow. The chart does not include a separate legend or explicit numerical percentage labels; instead, text labels are placed directly inside the slices, with some text rotated or significantly scaled down to fit within the smaller segments. There are no visually emphasized, exploded, or offset slices, and the segments do not appear to be strictly ordered by size within their respective parent categories. A small, solid grey rectangle is positioned in the blank center hole of the chart.
